questions: Is the limp you have causing pain in your leg, hip, or back when you walk?
Did this walking difficulty start suddenly, or did it come on slowly over weeks/months?
Have you had any injury to your lower body (leg, hip, spine) in the recent past?
Has anyone ever told you that one of your hips is "out of place" or abnormal on an X-ray?
Did you notice this walking pattern getting worse over months, or have you walked this way for as long as you can remember?
Do you have any weakness in your arms or difficulty climbing stairs?
Did you ever have a serious illness as a child that affected your legs, such as polio or a high fever with leg weakness?
Did your parents or anyone notice anything unusual about how you walked when you were learning to walk as a toddler?
Have you noticed any numbness or tingling in your legs?
Are the X-ray results available yet?
Do you have any family members who also walk with a limp or have hip problems?
When you squat down and stand back up, do you need to use your hands on your legs to push yourself up?
Can you stand on your left leg alone and keep your balance without your pelvis dropping?
Do you notice your left thigh muscle getting smaller or weaker compared to your right?
Have you had any steroid medication or long periods of bed rest in the past year?
Does your hip ever "click" or "catch" when you move it through certain positions?
Does your leg ever feel like it might "give way" or feel unstable?
Do you have any pain when sitting for a long time or when getting up from a low chair?
orders: Test passive range of motion of both hips, specifically checking for internal rotation and abduction limitations
Measure leg lengths (both true and apparent)
Perform a Trendelenburg test (have the patient stand on one leg at a time and observe pelvic stability)
Anteroposterior pelvis and both hips X-ray (please re-order, this is essential for diagnosis)
MRI of the left hip and pelvis to evaluate the gluteus medius tendon and acetabular anatomy
Flexion-adduction-internal rotation stress test of both hips to assess for femoral-acetabular impingement

ASK:
1. When you look down at your hips, does one side look higher or lower than the other?
2. Have you ever had an X-ray of your hips taken at any point in your life (perhaps during a routine check-up)?
3. Does your family come from a region or background where hip screening in babies is not routinely performed?
